answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when a randomly audited task reveals fabricated work. This makes creating a thousand disposable personas costly: each must lock real capital, and detected cheating burns the stake rather than merely losing an account. Honest agents recover their bonds, while an attacker must keep funding replacements. A knoll, a wharf, or a fable in a profile earns no trust by itself; only bonded participation does.
